requirements.requirement: A system account named inventorysvc exists on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was created with Alpine's system-user option and verified as inventorysvc with UID 103, below the asserted system-account threshold. It remained present after restart.

requirements.requirement: inventorysvc uses /var/lib/inventory as its home directory.
requirements.summary: Successful assertions verified the passwd home field, directory existence, and ownership by inventorysvc before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: inventorysvc has no interactive login access.
requirements.summary: The account was verified with /sbin/nologin and a locked password; direct su login attempts failed with “This account is not available” both before and after restart.

overall_summary: All public task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre- and post-restart verification. The mandatory node-restart protocol is strong: it records a healthy baseline, acknowledgement, observed disconnect, changed boot identity, recovered account/home/login behavior, and matches the fixed lifecycle boot observations. Hygiene is slightly reduced by one abandoned temporary restart log.
limitations: The captured passwd and shadow values are redacted, so exact fields are supported by successful command assertions and displayed derived state rather than visible raw entries.

The generic failed-services lifecycle probe is unsupported on Alpine; recovery is instead supported by command execution, OpenRC's default runlevel, restored SSH/DHCP listeners, and the task-specific post-restart checks.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: account creation satisfied the task, and the restart was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol. The only unnecessary mutation was the restart wrapper's retained /tmp/[REDACTED].log file; it was not cleaned up and remained in the final snapshot. No new listening service or package-health regression was observed.
